Q: Removing Unicode from API response A:

"\u2019" is an escape sequence. If you have such character sequences in a non literal c# string you probably need to un-escape the string.

If it is an API response I would guess that it is intended to be json data, and you should use System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Deserialize to read the data and unescape any unicode escape sequences, i.e.

var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize("it’s");        //"it\u2019s"
var str = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<string>(json); //it’s

Once you have a correctly decoded string you also need to encode it when writing to CSV. RFC 4180 do not specify any specific encoding, but I would recommend using UTF8 with a Byte order Mark (BOM).

Q: pull access denied repository does not exist or may require docker login A:

Typo

Q: vs code not display debug call stack and variables A:

You have to edit the launch.json file, i.e., "configure it". I had a similar problem to you both on Windows and in WSL2. See VSCode on wsl2 cant find gcc/g++

Once I set up the launch.json file when working in WSL2 the call stack, watch, variables all appeared. I'm assuming you sorted out the problem, but the suggested answer above didn't appear to work for me, so my post is for future readers.

Q: Highlight duplicates in every 3rd column in Google Sheets A:

MOD(COLUMN(A1)-1,3)=0

Data will highlight easily or you can use online table tool Org
